Title: a. Program Evaluations:  A+ Scholarship, Library Media

fields.Content:
District programs are evaluated annually or biennially per Policy IM. These evaluations assess progress toward meeting established goals and provide recommendations for improvement. The evaluation process ensures that programs remain effective, aligned with district goals, and responsive to the needs of students and the community.

Program evaluations are summarized and formalized for the Board of Education to maintain transparency and accountability. These updates provide the Board with a clear understanding of program progress and areas for improvement, facilitating informed decision-making.

Program Evaluations for the A+ Scholarship Program, the Library Media Centers, and the 2024-25 Program Evaluation Schedule are attached in Supporting documents.
Approve the A+ Scholarship Program and Library Media program evaluations as presented.

As part of the district’s assessment plan, students are assessed using iReady in reading and math three times per year in grades K-12, except for high school students who receive on or above grade level on the fall assessment. Those students are exempt from the winter testing window. High school students are assessed in all English classes for reading and students in Algebra I, Algebra II, and Geometry are given the mathematics assessment

Phonics and Word Recognition Survey (PWRS) is an assessment part of the Language Essentials for Teachers of Reading and Spelling (LETRS). The survey measures phonics and word reading recognition. Students in grades K-5 are given the survey once per quarter (four times per year). The data is used by teachers to monitor students' progress.

Each year the Board of Education sets the calendar for the following school year.  The goal has been to get the calendar set as soon as practical so that families and community can plan appropriately.  

Districts are required to provide 1044 hours of student attendance, with a minimum number of 169 student attendance days.  School calendars must also include 36 make-up hours for inclement weather, for a total of at least 1080 hours.  The proposed 2025-2026 calendar has 1084.5 student hours (165 full days and 4 half days) plus the 36 hours (6 days) for inclement weather or other emergencies.  This exceeds the number of state required hours in order to maintain approximately the same amount of student instructional time as the current and previous years.  Districts are required to start no sooner than 14 days prior to the first Monday in September. 

The proposed calendar is substantially similar to the 2024-25 calendar except that Spring Break starts on the 5th Monday rather than the 4th Monday to align with the Herndon Center calendar.  The proposed calendar has 188 contracted days for teachers which  includes five paid holidays and a flexed day for parent/teacher conferences, four additional days for new teachers' orientation, 169 days for student attendance and includes the additional built-in 36 hours for make-up days.

District Potpourri met several times this fall and sought feedback from employees at their sites.  Potpourri supports recommending the final proposed 2025-26 calendar and narrative, which can be found in Supporting Documents, to the Board of Education for approval.
Approve the calendar for school year 2025-2026 as presented in Supporting Documents.
